text:
Matt H: heads-up, noticed a weird routing/compat edge where clients sending both X-API-Version and X-Client-Version get routed inconsistently. Some tenants end up on v1 fallback even though they opted into v2.
Sara V: hmm, do you have an example header blob?
Matt H: yep — reproducer from curl: `curl -H \"X-API-Version: v2\" -H \"X-Client-Version: 1.9.0\" https://api.redwood.ai/generate` -> goes to v1 pool.
Lee C: that's the old precedence logic kicking in. We check token metadata, then headers, then fallback. If token lacks version affinity we use a cheap entropy hash that sometimes matches legacy tenants.
Jordan P: is this causing quota mischarging or just routing noise?
Matt H: mostly routing noise + a couple of support tickets where customers saw higher tail latency (v1) unexpectedly. Also console shows mixed telemetry which confused canary dashboards.
Sara V: can we short-term change the header precedence? e.g., prefer X-API-Version over token map for 2 weeks while we backfill tokens?
Lee C: we could, but that would alter routing for many tenants and might break things relying on token affinity. Need a safe opt-in path.
Matt H: proposal: add a \"header-strict\" probe cohort. If a tenant sets `console.flag: header-strict=true` then routing honors header over token. Keep default unchanged.
Jordan P: sounds good. We should also emit a telemetry counter when header wins vs token wins so dashboards show impact. Metric names: `routing.header_override.count` and tag `result:header|token|fallback`.
Sara V: +1 for telemetry. Can we sample 1% tenant traffic automatically for 48h to gauge impact (no changing of routing)? Ops team can attach sampling tag.
Lee C: sampling only (read-only) is safe; we can log the would-be-routing choice in the debug span: `routing.would_have.v2` boolean. Low overhead if sampled.
Matt H: ok plan concrete steps: 1) add would_have telemetry & sampling (Lee) 2) add console UI to opt into header-strict for a tenant (Sara) 3) rollout header-strict to a small cohort and monitor metrics (Jordan) 4) decide full flip after 2 weeks of signals.
Jordan P: on quotas — if we flip header precedence some tenants might shift from Dedicated -> Shared pools and hit different quota buckets. Need a preflight alert: `quota.tenant_pool_shift` and a dashboard showing estimated delta.
Lee C: we can compute estimated cost delta using recent routing distribution and capacity classes. I can add a nightly job that projects the 7-day delta per tenant if header precedence were flipped.
Sara V: dashboard widgets: projected active sessions delta, 95/99 latency delta, token billing delta. Add links to runbook and a toggle to schedule migration.
Matt H: runbook note: if a tenant hits unexpected quota after flip, console should auto-fallback them to previous affinity for 30m and page oncall. Add `console.auto_fallback=true` as a safety.
ops-bot: Created issue #ENG-4321: \"header-strict probe + telemetry + console opt-in\" and assigned to @Lee C, @Sara V. ETA: 5 days for probe + dashboard draft.
Sara V: I'll lay out the console UX mockups tonight — keeping the opt-in on tenant settings page with a small tooltip explaining risks.
Lee C: implementation notes: add a config flag `routing.header_precedence_override` (per-tenant, boolean) and wire it into router decision path. Also emit `routing.decision_source` in traces.
Jordan P: add a short sampling kql we can paste in dashboard: ``query: logs | where routing_decision_source == \"would_have_header\" | stats count() by tenant_id``
Matt H: perf check: do not enable would_have logging for >5% of requests — keep sampling low to avoid blow-up.
Sara V: agreed. I'll add a console control to set sampling rate (0.1%/1%/5%).
Lee C: risk: clients that intentionally send both headers (bad clients) could still be ambiguous. We should add guidance in client docs: prefer single version header and advise pinning token metadata.
Jordan P: final question — do we want an automated graceback if smart-routing causes errors? e.g., if error rate > 2x baseline for a tenant, revert routing decision and notify.
Matt H: yes, automated rollback threshold + alert. Add to runbook: rollback trigger = sustained 2x errors over 5m or 3% absolute increase in error rate.
Sara V: I'll update dashboard alerts and create a preflight checklist.
Matt H: thanks everyone. I'll leave the issue open and mark owners. We'll sync in the ops call tomorrow. :thumbsup:
